3. The present Application under Section 379 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (B.N.S.S.),
2023, has been filed on behalf of the applicant/respondent No. 2, namely, Smt. Rakhi.

4. It is submitted in the application that the petitioner has filed the Main Petition bearing CRL.M.C.
3880/2024, for quashing of the FIR No. 88/2021 under Section 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC, 1860'), registered at Police Station Ranjeet Nagar, on account of the Settlement dated 26.04.2024.
However, as per the terms of the Settlement, the petitioner had agreed to pay a total sum of Rs.7,50,000/-, out This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/08/2024 at 22:27:11 of which Rs.20,000/- were paid by way of bank transfer and Rs.50,000/- in cash, leaving a balance of Rs.3,80,000/-.

The petitioner issued a cheque bearing No. 526770 dated 26.04.2024, drawn on IDBI Bank, for the payment of Rs.3,80,000/- but on presentation, the cheqe was dishonoured due to the signatures being different.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent No. 2, issued Legal Notice to the brother-in-law of the petitioner, who had isused the cheque on behalf of the petiotner and requested him to clear the cheque, as had been agreed by the parties.
Though the petiotner has sought quashing but has failed to abide by the terms of the Settlement and while filing the main Petition for quashing has remained silent about the dishonour of the cheque.

It is claimed that even the Judge, Family Court, Delhi, in its Order dated 06.06.2024 had observed that the petitioner is misleading the Court and he despite the service, failed to appear in the Execution Petition and NBWs have been issued against him.
The petitioner has appeared in the Execution Petition but has been seeking time to make the payment.
6. It is submitted that while consealing the material facts, a stay Order was granted by this Court on 14.06.2024, on the submissions made by the petitioner as the matter has been amicably settled.
It is submitted that the stay is liable to be vacated.

The prayer is made that the FIR under the various provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (B.N.S.S.) 2023, be directed to be registered for the offences committed by the petitioner.
7.
Submissions heard.
8. The averments made in the present Petition, is that the cheque that was given for the part amount of Settlement as agreed between the parties, has got dishonoured.
The respondent herein is at liberty to approach the
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/08/2024 at 22:27:11 appropriate forum to seek the redressal in regard to the dishonour of the cheque or other provisions of B.N.S.S, 2023.
9.
The Application is accordingly disposed of.

CRL.M.C. 3880/2024 (under Section 482 CrPC filed by the petitioner for quashing of FIR No.
0088/2021 dated 27.04.2021 under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC, registered at P.S. Ranjeet Nagar)

10. The present Petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, 1973, has been filed on behalf of the petiotner for quashing of the FIR No. 0088/2021 dated 27.04.2021 for the offence under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC, 1860, registered at PS Ranjeet Nagar.

11. Since the petitioner has failed to honour the Settlement in full and has failed to pay the part Settlement amount i.e. Rs.3,80,000/-, which remains to be paid, it cannot be said that the matter stands fully settled especially when the same is being opposed by the respondent.
12. The Petition is hereby dismissed with liberty to the petitioner, to seek quashing in case the parties arrived at a Settlement in future.
13. The Petition is disposed of.
